scan_metadata.explanation: Both filtered tutorials matched. They demonstrate one coherent workflow: list/choose a model, annotate a log1p-normalised (1e4) AnnData ('best match' or 'prob match', optional majority voting), export labels/probabilities, compare predictions with an existing label column (celltypist.dotplot, pd.crosstab, per-group probability boxplots), train a custom model from a labelled reference, and inspect a model's top driving genes. Duplicate demonstrations (built-in vs custom model, best vs prob match, two tutorials) were merged into 5 exposed tools across two modules: celltypist_tutorial owns 4 and celltypist_tutorial_ml owns 1. Model download, AnnData/table conversion, demo-data download and UMAP embedding plots are internal or omitted. Selecting a tool does not establish that it runs; the environment and execution stages decide that.

tutorials.title: Using CellTypist for cell type classification
tutorials.description: Annotates demo_2000_cells with the built-in Immune_All_Low.pkl model (best match + majority voting), converts results to AnnData, compares with the existing 'cell_type' column via celltypist.dotplot, trains a custom model on demo_2000_cells (feature_selection=True), predicts demo_400_cells with it, and inspects top driving genes (Mast cells) with violin plots.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Matches the explicit tutorial filter. Covers the core user tasks (model listing, annotation, reference comparison, training, marker inspection) on public Sanger-hosted demo data (demo_2000_cells, demo_400_cells).

tutorials.title: Using CellTypist for multi-label classification
tutorials.description: Annotates demo_500_cells (includes novel 'Microglia' and in-silico doublet 'Macro_pDC') with Immune_All_Low.pkl in 'best match' and 'prob match' (p_thres=0.5) modes with majority voting, inserts probabilities with to_adata(insert_prob=True), compares with 'cell_type' via pd.crosstab and celltypist.dotplot (predicted_labels and majority_voting), trains a custom model on demo_2000_cells, predicts demo_500 in prob-match mode, shows per-group probability boxplots, and extracts top driving genes (Macrophages).
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Matches the explicit tutorial filter. It is the only source that demonstrates multi-label 'prob match' mode, insert_prob, both use_as_prediction variants of the dotplot, the reference-vs-prediction crosstab, and the per-reference-group probability boxplots.

tool_review.task: Assign per-cell CellTypist labels to a user's log1p-normalised (1e4 counts/cell) scRNA-seq AnnData using a built-in model name or a user .pkl model. Supports best-match single labels or prob-match multi-labels ('A|B', 'Unassigned'), optional majority voting over over-clustering, and returns probabilities and confidence scores.

inputs.adata_path: h5ad; .X (or .raw.X) log1p-normalised to 1e4 counts/cell, gene symbols as var_names. Upstream Classifier.__init__ falls back to .raw.X when .X looks scaled, raises ValueError when both are invalid, and warns when the first cell's expm1 sum differs from 1e4 by more than 1.
inputs.model: str, default 'Immune_All_Low.pkl' (upstream default via models.json 'default': true). Accepts a built-in filename or an absolute path to a .pkl written by celltypist_train_model.
inputs.p_thres: float, default 0.5; used only in prob match
inputs.majority_voting: bool. Upstream default is False; both tutorials use True. Keep the upstream default and test with True.
inputs.optional_upstream_params_if_tested: over_clustering (obs column key of user clusters, e.g. PBMC3k 'louvain'), min_prop (default 0), insert_conf_by ('predicted_labels'|'majority_voting', README). Each is an existing annotate()/to_adata() argument; expose one only when it is tested.

tool_review.outputs: annotated.h5ad: input obs plus predicted_labels, over_clustering and majority_voting when majority voting ran, and conf_score; when majority voting ran it also holds the neighbor graph and X_pca. Also predicted_labels.csv, probability_matrix.csv and decision_matrix.csv via to_table, and a concise summary: n_cells, model used, whether majority voting ran, and label counts via AnnotationResult.summary_frequency(by=...).

symbols: celltypist.annotate(filename, model, mode, p_thres, majority_voting, over_clustering, min_prop)
models.download_models(model=<name>) (internal, only for a built-in name not yet cached)

io_adaptations: Model handling. For a built-in name, call models.download_models(model=name) before annotate when $CELLTYPIST_FOLDER/data/models/<name> is missing. Otherwise Model.load(name) calls get_all_models(), whose download_if_required() downloads all 61 models when the cache holds no .pkl.

For a custom model, pass an absolute path. Model.load only skips the name lookup when the string contains '/' (models.py:84-87); a bare relative 'x.pkl' goes through get_all_models() and can trigger the same download-all.
Report when majority voting was skipped: annotate warns and returns no majority_voting column when n_cells <= 50 (annotate.py:89-91).

annotate mutates the AnnData it is given: over_cluster writes X_pca, connectivities, distances and uns['neighbors'], and to_adata writes obs columns. An existing neighbor graph in the input h5ad is reused, not rebuilt (classifier.py over_cluster; the ml tutorial cell 55 log shows 'Detected a neighborhood graph'). A processed PBMC3k h5ad will therefore over-cluster on the user's own graph. That is upstream behaviour; document it, do not change it.

Composition contract (to be fixed by the celltypist_tutorial implementer and consumed by celltypist_tutorial_ml): annotate writes <out>/predicted_labels.csv, decision_matrix.csv and probability_matrix.csv via AnnotationResult.to_table(folder=out), and <out>/annotated.h5ad via AnnotationResult.to_adata() with default insert_prob=False. The CSV index is obs_names. Keep the probability/decision matrices in CSV, not in obs: insert_prob=True adds one obs column per model cell type, and many Immune_All_Low names contain '/' (e.g. 'CD8a/a', 'HSC/MPP'). anndata 0.13 then emits a FutureWarning, or raises ValueError when settings.disallow_forward_slash_in_h5ad is set (anndata/_io/specs/registry.py:394-401). Those columns can also overwrite existing obs columns of the same name.

tool_review.task: Train a custom CellTypist logistic-regression model from a labelled reference AnnData, optionally with SGD-based feature selection, and save it as .pkl for annotation or marker inspection.

inputs.adata_path: h5ad, log1p-normalised to 1e4 (check_expression=True upstream; raw.X is used when X has negative values)
inputs.label_key: Required obs column holding training labels (the tutorial demo uses 'cell_type'). Validate that it exists; do not hard-code it.
inputs.feature_selection: bool. Upstream default is False; the tutorial uses True. Keep the upstream default and test with True.
inputs.random_state: Optional int, forwarded through train(**kwargs) to SGDClassifier and LogisticRegression; both accept it. The tutorials did not set it.
inputs.optional_upstream_params_if_tested: use_SGD, C, max_iter, check_expression, details/source/version description strings
inputs.output_path: Fresh per-call directory. Model.write forces a .pkl extension. Return an absolute path for use by celltypist_annotate_cells and celltypist_inspect_model.

tool_review.outputs: Absolute model .pkl path. Summary: cell types, number of features, number of non-expressed genes filtered (train() logs this but does not return it; compute it as the count of zero-sum columns only if needed), and the model description dict.

With a fixed random_state, two calls give identical features and coef_.
Model.write followed by Model.load round-trips cell_types, features and coef_.

Top-3 markers from the trained model: Mast cells ['TPSB2','TPSAB1','CPA3'] (main cell 66), Macrophages ['EREG','AQP9','OLR1'] (ml cell 89). Expected to be robust, but compare by set overlap unless a seed is fixed.

tool_review.nondeterminism: With feature_selection=True the first round uses SGDClassifier(random_state=None by default; train.py _SGDClassifier), so the selected gene set differs between runs. The two tutorials' identical calls selected 2607 vs 2619 genes. The second round, LogisticRegression lbfgs, is deterministic given the features. n_jobs does not change results once random_state is fixed.
tool_review.blockers: train.py _LRClassifier passes LogisticRegression(multi_class='ovr'). scikit-learn 1.7.2's docstring says multi_class 'was deprecated in version 1.5 and will be removed in 1.8', so scikit-learn must be <1.8. reports/environment-manager_results.md confirms that 1.8.0 and 1.9.1 raise TypeError and that the env is pinned to 1.7.2. tool_review.task: Quantify how CellTypist predictions (raw predicted_labels or majority_voting) agree with an existing label or cluster column in the user's data: a label-transfer dot plot, a contingency table, and, for selected reference groups such as suspected novel or doublet clusters, the distribution of per-cell-type probabilities.
tool_review.decision_reasoning: This is a selected scientific output. Both tutorials present the dotplot as the 'more useful way' to evaluate predictions (main cell 40, ml cell 48), and the intended use case (PBMC3k with author labels) has existing labels. The reference column is a required parameter (reference_key) that is never hard-coded to 'cell_type'. It is a separate tool so a user can compare predicted_labels and majority_voting, or several reference columns, without re-running annotation and over-clustering.

inputs.annotation_dir: Output directory of celltypist_annotate_cells: predicted_labels.csv, probability_matrix.csv, decision_matrix.csv and annotated.h5ad. Explicit file paths are an equivalent alternative.
inputs.reference_key: Required obs column in annotated.h5ad (tutorial demo: 'cell_type'; PBMC3k: e.g. 'louvain'). Validate that it exists; upstream raises KeyError.
inputs.use_as_prediction: 'majority_voting' (upstream default) | 'predicted_labels'. Upstream raises KeyError when majority_voting is absent.
inputs.probability_groups: Optional list of reference_key values that get probability boxplots (the tutorial demo used 'Microglia' and 'Macro_pDC'). Validate that each exists.

tool_review.outputs: Dot-plot PNG. Dot fraction table and mean-probability table (the plotted values; read from the DotPlot returned with return_fig=True as dp.dot_size_df / dp.dot_color_df, or confirm equivalence with the dotplot inputs). Crosstab CSV (reference x prediction). Optional per-group boxplot PNGs.

tool_review.reason: Setup with network side effects. Download only the named model on demand with download_models(model=name). Do not download all models: the tutorial's download_models(force_update=True) now fetches 61 models (12 at tutorial time). models_path is fixed at import from $CELLTYPIST_FOLDER (default ~/.celltypist), and importing celltypist creates that directory. Set CELLTYPIST_FOLDER to a project-controlled cache (the project has tmp/celltypist_home) before importing celltypist.

Serialization and loading, used inside annotate, train and inspect. to_table and summary_frequency are documented in the README, not demonstrated in the filtered tutorials; use them only as upstream helpers for output files and a concise summary.

tool_review.reason: Demonstration visualization. Generic scanpy embedding plots are not part of the CellTypist method. The quantitative agreement output is the dotplot/crosstab in celltypist_compare_with_reference. annotated.h5ad keeps the neighbor graph (and X_pca) built for over-clustering so users can compute their own embedding. Users with existing embeddings, such as PBMC3k X_umap, already have one. UMAP coordinates are also version-dependent, so they are a weak verification target. The figures stay as reference evidence for executors.
